pk.context: 60 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Food increases Cmax by 12% to 55% and AUC by 9% to 37%. Protein binding is 96% to 99%, and the drug is extensively metabolized in the liver.
clues.substance: The active moiety has a molecular weight of 369.4. It is a crystalline powder that melts with decomposition at 140°C.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 30 mg and 60 mg delayed-release capsules, dosed once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to any component and with rilpivirine-containing products; diarrhea and abdominal pain are common.
clues.indication: Healing of erosive esophagitis of all grades, maintenance of healing with relief of heartburn, and symptomatic non-erosive reflux disease, in patients 12 years and older.
clues.mechanism: Specifically inhibits the (H+, K+)-ATPase at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell, blocking the final step of acid production.

tell: A proton pump inhibitor whose dual delayed-release granules give two separate plasma concentration peaks.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: the first peak occurs one to two hours after administration
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: eliminated with a half-life of approximately one to two hours in healthy subjects
